title: Generic types and methods
hook: A generic type names T on the type. A generic method names T on the method. The compiler infers method type arguments from the call; you still close types when you new them up.

sections.heading: Declaring and closing
sections.prose: class CacheClient<T> is an open generic. CacheClient<SessionDto> is closed. You can nest: Dictionary<string, List<Message>>. Static fields of CacheClient<T> are per closed T — CacheClient<int> and CacheClient<string> do not share a static dictionary. That fact has bitten more than one “global stats” counter. Generic methods live on ordinary or generic types: static void Print<T>(T value). At the call site Print(42) infers T as int. Sometimes inference fails (when T appears only in the return type); then you write Parse<Message>(json).

snippets.label: Type plus method
snippets.explanation: RedisCache<T> closes T at construction. GetOrAdd infers TKey/TValue from the dictionary. notnull on TKey matches Dictionary’s own constraint.

sections.heading: Inference and overloads
sections.prose: Inference uses arguments, not assignments (mostly). var x = Empty<int>(); needs the type argument because nothing is passed. Collection expressions and target typing (C# 12+) can close a generic from the left-hand side: List<string> names = ["a"];. Overloaded generic methods are a compiler puzzle; if the interview goes there, prefer simplifying signatures over memorizing spec tie-breakers.

sections.heading: Interfaces, structs, records, delegates
sections.prose: IComparable<T>, IEnumerable<T>, Func<T, TResult>, Task<T>, EventHandler<TEventArgs> are generic. You can declare generic records and generic structs. A generic struct still lives on the stack when it is a local (subject to the usual lifting in async). Do not make a giant generic God-class that takes ten type parameters; that is a missed opportunity to split.

interviewTakeaways: Open versus closed generic types; static state is per closed type.
Generic methods infer from arguments; specify T when they cannot.
Dictionary<TKey, TValue> is the canonical multi-parameter generic.
commonPitfalls: Assuming static fields on Generic<T> are shared across all T.
Fighting inference instead of writing Foo<T>(...) explicitly.
Putting T on the class when only one method needed it.

jsTsCorrelations.note: TS infers similarly from arguments. There is no per-T static field because there is no runtime T.
